rules_changelog.v2: Direction fix: 'प्राप्त हुए', 'mile hain', 'credit ho jayega', 'received from' no longer count as money-in by themselves; they need the user named as recipient or a non-user sender in the same sentence. Found via a benign Hindi bill-receipt template (merchant_bill_hi_07) hitting the amount-mismatch floor; because it was found by looking at evaluation failures, the separate validation set is the cleaner check that it generalises. Measured effect on synthetic data: benign hard-floor hits 6 -> 0 (all merchant_bill_hi_07); scam hard-floor hits unchanged (231); digital_arrest_hien_01 loses reward_claim on 10 rows ('drugs mile hain' = 'drugs were found', which v1 misread as money-in).

data.text: UCI SMS Spam (public, English, UK 2000s) + Vyakhya synthetic en/hi/hi-en (generator v2)
data.transaction: public synthetic mobile-money data (PaySim), not UPI; sender history from Vyakhya synthetic transactions

disclaimer: All metrics come from synthetic and public datasets (UCI SMS Spam, Vyakhya synthetic messages, PaySim). They are not production accuracy.
